evals.name: conversation-to-blog-post
evals.prompt:
Turn this session into a blog post.

Summary: We migrated our CI pipeline from GitHub Actions self-hosted runners to a hybrid setup where heavy builds run on AWS spot instances and lightweight checks stay on GitHub-hosted runners. Key decisions: used Packer to bake AMIs with pre-warmed Docker layers, brought build times from 14 minutes to 3 minutes, and saved ~$400/month by eliminating always-on runners. The pattern we discovered: pre-warming the build environment is cheaper than keeping runners alive. We hit one snag where spot instance termination left dangling build artifacts in S3 — solved with a lifecycle policy that expires incomplete uploads after 1 hour.

assertions.text: Output Markdown file has valid frontmatter with slug, title, description, date, hidden, and tags fields
Written in first-person conversational tone, not third-person documentation style
Uses --- horizontal rules to separate major sections
Opens with the problem or motivation, not warm-up fluff
Ends with a "Bottom line" or "What's next" section
Includes concrete numbers from the session (14→3 min, $400/month savings)
